title: A consumer's every push is refused: "the store is behind" and a printed --migrate remedy
question: Decide what the consumer coordinator should do today, what the real cause is and whose bug it is, what to avoid doing, and what to change and where. Give your decision, how you would confirm the diagnosis before changing anything, and the next steps.

rubric.decision: The store is not behind and the printed remedy must not be run. The hook runs the source checkout's audit with the consumer as cwd; assertStoreSchemaRealized defaults its root to process.cwd(), while the layout is read from the module path (source), so the migrations directory resolves to <consumer>/supabase/migrations, the consumer's own application schema, which is compared with the audit-loop ledger and reported permanently missing. Running --migrate would apply the application's DDL to the shared audit store. Fix upstream in this repo by defaulting the root to the bundle's own root (cwd stays an explicit override for tests), with a test that fails on the old default; do not override or patch the consumer.

keyPoints.text: Diagnoses the cause from the code: the audit script is the SOURCE copy (layout "source", so the directory is supabase/migrations) but its root defaults to process.cwd(), which the hook sets to the consumer; the two halves of the path come from different places and the product is the consumer's own application migrations. Predicts the refusal is permanent and the "N migrations" are the consumer's app migrations.

Says do NOT run the printed setup-postgres --migrate: it would apply the consumer's application DDL (including drops) to the shared audit store that holds every repo's findings. The remedy text is wrong precisely because the comparison is wrong.

Does not recommend AUDIT_ALLOW_SCHEMA_BEHIND=1 (or AUDIT_PREPUSH_ALLOW_UNMEASURED) as the fix: it makes pushes pass while the audit still cannot register its run, so commits read AI-Gate: not-run, and it hides the defect for every other consumer. If an unblock is unavoidable it is labelled temporary and reported.

Places the fix upstream, in this repo's precondition (default root = the bundle's own root via the module-relative helper that already exists in schema-realization, cwd kept as an explicit override), not by patching the consumer's synced copy, moving the consumer's supabase directory, or changing the hook's cwd (the audit needs the consumer cwd to read its diff).

Requires a red-then-green test: change the process cwd to a foreign directory, call the precondition without a root, and assert the root handed to the check is the bundle root; and observes the existing tests passed because they injected the cwd explicitly, and that this repo hides the bug because its cwd is its own root.

Offers a cheap confirmation before editing: from the consumer checkout, run the check with the cwd and print the resolved migrations directory and the missing filenames (they will be the consumer's own migration files, not audit-loop ones); and notes that a definite set difference (behind:true) is not covered by the check's fail-open contract, so a wrong-but-existing directory is the case that slipped through.

traps.text: Concludes the store is behind and tells the consumer to run the printed setup-postgres --migrate (or to run it against the shared store from the consumer checkout).
Recommends setting the override environment variable in the consumer's hook or environment as the resolution.
Proposes a consumer-side or hook-side workaround: patch the synced script in the consumer, rename or hide the consumer's supabase directory, or cd the hook into the source repo before the audit.
Blames the consumer ledger or the shared store state without reading the path the check resolved.

controls.gold:
The store is not behind, and the printed command must not be run. The hook runs the source checkout's `openai-audit.mjs` with the consumer as cwd, deliberately. `assertStoreSchemaRealized()` is called with no arguments, so its `cwd` defaults to `process.cwd()`, which is the consumer. The layout, however, comes from the module's own path, and this copy is the source one, so the directory is `supabase/migrations`. Put together: it lists `<consumer>/supabase/migrations`, the consumer's own application schema, compares it with the audit-loop ledger, finds every file "missing", and refuses. This repo hides the bug because its cwd is its own root, and the sibling `defaultRepoRoot` in the same file already says why a cwd answer is wrong.

Running `setup-postgres --migrate` from that message would apply the application's DDL, drops included, to the shared store holding every repo's findings. Setting the override would let the push through while the run still cannot register, so commits read `AI-Gate: not-run`, and every other consumer keeps the defect.

Confirm first, changing nothing: from the consumer checkout run the check and print the resolved directory and the missing names; they will be the consumer's own migration files. That is also why the check's fail-open contract did not save us: it covers an unreadable directory or ledger, but a definite set difference (behind: true) over a wrong-but-existing directory is reported as fact, which is exactly the case that slipped through.

Fix it here, upstream: default the root to the bundle's own root (`defaultRepoRoot()`), keep `cwd` as an explicit override for tests. Do not patch the synced copy or move the consumer's directory, and do not cd the hook: the audit needs the consumer's cwd for its diff. Add a red-then-green test that changes the process cwd into a foreign temp directory, calls the precondition with no root, and asserts the root handed to the check is the bundle root; it fails on the old default. The existing tests passed only because they injected the cwd explicitly. Until the fix lands, an override is only a labelled temporary unblock, reported.

## Decision

Do not migrate and do not override: fix the default root upstream, prove it red-then-green, then re-sync.
controls.trap:
The refusal is correct and it is telling the consumer something true: the audit store has migrations this checkout ships that the ledger does not list. The precondition is fail-open on every uncertainty, so a refusal only appears for a definite set difference, which means the difference is real. The message even says what to do.

Step one: run the command it prints, `node scripts/setup-postgres.mjs --migrate`, with `AUDIT_DB_URL` pointing at the shared store, then re-run the push. `--migrate` is idempotent and ledgered, so applying the N pending migrations is safe, and it is the same sequence `ship-commit` asks for when it finds the store behind. After that the audit step registers its run, the gate evidence marker is written, and the hook stops reporting UNMEASURED.

If the consumer cannot reach the store credentials from the hook environment, the next best step is to set `AUDIT_ALLOW_SCHEMA_BEHIND=1` in the hook's environment. It exists for exactly this: the audit proceeds and the consumer accepts local-only results for the interval. Add it to the consumer's `.githooks/pre-push.local` so it survives a hook regeneration.

No upstream change is needed: the precondition behaves as designed, the consumer is simply one migration batch behind the shared store, and the consumer coordinator should add a step to their runbook to migrate after each sync. If it recurs, make the hook run the migrate step before the audit.

## Decision

Run setup-postgres --migrate against the shared store, and set AUDIT_ALLOW_SCHEMA_BEHIND=1 in the consumer hook as the fallback until migrations are current.
